newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent falls with NYMEX as Iraq tensions ease.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent falls with NYMEX as Iraq tensions ease.

text.p: SIMEX Brent November futures fell on Monday in moderate trading, tracking the decline on NYMEX crude futures as tensions in the Gulf appeared to ease.
November was last traded at $22.65 per barrel, down 48 cents from London's close on Friday of $23.13.
November volume was 60 lots in late trading. The Brent October contract expired on Friday.
Brokers said they expected initial support for the market to strike at $22.50, but some said the slide could add another $1.00 through the week so long as Iraqi tensions continued to ease.
NYMEX November crude was last traded on the after-hours ACCESS system at $23.50 per barrel, down 44 cents from New York's close on Friday of $23.94.
NYMEX October, which expires on Friday, was last traded at $24.05, down 46 cents from New York.
NYMEX fell on Friday in response to Iraq's announcement that it planned to cease firing at U.S. and allied warplanes patrolling the no-fly zones in the country.
